definitions.explanation: The end of a fiscal or academic year. In Japan, the fiscal year typically ends on March 31st, making late March a particularly busy time for businesses and schools.

examples.japanese: {年度末|ねんどまつ}は{忙|いそが}しい。
examples.english: The end of the fiscal year is busy.

examples.japanese: {年度末|ねんどまつ}までに{予算|よさん}を{使|つか}い{切|き}る。
examples.english: Use up the budget by the end of the fiscal year.

examples.japanese: {年度末|ねんどまつ}の{決算|けっさん}{処理|しょり}に{追|お}われている。
examples.english: I'm swamped with year-end accounting work.

notes:
WORD FORMATION:
{年度|ねんど} (fiscal/academic year) + {末|まつ} (end)

JAPANESE FISCAL YEAR:
In Japan, the fiscal year ({会計年度|かいけいねんど}) runs from April 1st to March 31st. The academic year follows the same pattern. This makes late March ({年度末|ねんどまつ}) extremely busy.

COMMON ACTIVITIES:
- {決算|けっさん} (financial closing)
- {予算|よさん}{消化|しょうか} (budget utilization)
- {人事異動|じんじいどう} (personnel transfers)
- {卒業|そつぎょう}/{入学|にゅうがく} (graduation/enrollment)

RELATED TERMS:
- {年度|ねんど}: fiscal year
- {年度始|ねんどはじ}め: beginning of fiscal year
- {期末|きまつ}: end of term/period
- {年末|ねんまつ}: end of calendar year
